audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Zaahen's ultimate locks you down, in five places: 'his R locks you down the moment you blink onto him', 'locks you with R if you blink in', 'Even scaled, his R locks you the moment you blink in', 'Lock you with R when you blink in', and the enemyWin row 'Zaahen wins by landing Ultimate'. The whole commit schedule is built on it.
audit.why: Grim Deliverance has no crowd control at all. Riot's text: 'Zaahen rises then stabs downward, damaging enemies and healing for a portion of the damage dealt' — its only derived flag is heal. The ability that actually catches a blinking Kassadin is Dreaded Return: 'Zaahen stabs in a direction, damaging enemies hit, then pulls them toward him', 850 range on 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 seconds. So the page tells you to schedule your only engage around a 110-second ultimate that cannot hold you, while the real catch tool is on fourteen seconds and reaches 850 units. That is the difference between committing safely and dying to a cooldown you were told to ignore.
audit.corrected: Grim Deliverance is a heal, not a lockdown. Dreaded Return is the pull that catches a blink — 14s at rank 1, 850 range — and it is the cooldown your commits should be scheduled around.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (R description and flags: heal only; W description, cooldown 14/13.5/13/12.5/12, range 850)

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one of Zaahen's five abilities is named anywhere on the page. Every string says 'his R', 'his physical damage', 'Ultimate'.
audit.why: This is the largest sample in the whole Kassadin slice — 1030 games — and it is the emptiest page. The names and numbers are all in the kit file: The Darkin Glaive (Q, 10/9/8/7/6s) slashes twice on his next attack and heals, and can be RECAST so the following attack knocks you up; Dreaded Return (W, 850 range) pulls; Aureate Rush (E, 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s) is his dash; Grim Deliverance (R, 110/95/80s, 600 range) heals him off its own damage. Two of those carry flagged interactions that also never appear: Q is an auto-attack reset, so the burst tell is the wind-up rather than a cast, and Aureate Rush carries percent-health damage, which means stacking health alone is not the answer to it.
audit.corrected: Name them: The Darkin Glaive (Q, 10s, auto-reset, heals, recast knocks up), Dreaded Return (W, 14s, 850 pull), Aureate Rush (E, 10s dash, percent-health), Grim Deliverance (R, 110s, heals).

audit.whatIsWrong: Cultivation of War is never mentioned, and it contains a revive.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Zaahen's attacks and abilities against enemy champions grant him stacks of Determination, gaining bonus Attack Damage per stack. When filled with Determination, Zaahen gains increased Attack Damage and can revive.' For a champion whose entire late-game plan is 'blink in, burst one target, blink out', an enemy who can come back from the kill is the single most important thing to know, and it is also a power spike that runs on stacks rather than on levels or items — so it is invisible to a level chart. The stacks come from hitting YOU, which means the long trades the page already tells you to refuse also charge his revive.
audit.corrected: Cultivation of War stacks Determination off every hit on a champion; a full bar gives bonus attack damage and lets him revive. Bursting him is not always killing him.

audit.why: Sides and ratings untouched, and they are well supported here — 47.38% over 1030 games is by far the strongest evidence in my slice and it agrees with a chart giving Zaahen six stages at 8/10 with Skill only at two-plus items. This is the one Kassadin matchup where the chart and the data clearly line up, so I changed nothing.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Level 6 restores some dignity' with no account of what Zaahen gets at 6.
audit.why: Grim Deliverance is 110/95/80 seconds at 600 range and heals him for a portion of the damage it deals. It arrives at the same level your Riftwalk does, and while it is not the lockdown the page imagines, it is a sustain spike that undoes a trade you thought you had won. A hundred and ten seconds at rank 1 is also a genuinely long window to play around once you know it exists.
audit.corrected: Grim Deliverance: 110s at rank 1, 600 range, and it heals him off the damage it deals. Never trade into a fresh one.

audit.why: Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield; it has never silenced in this kit version.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

audit.why: 47.38% over 1030 games. The page quotes no figure. No change — but this sample deserves a page that names his abilities, which is what the edits do.

edits.before: The problem is stark: your Null Sphere shield only blocks magic damage and everything he does is physical, so from level 2 he simply walks you down and denies your helpless pre-6 frame. Concede the trades, catch what CS you safely can, and lean on tower — every level survived without dying is a win.
edits.after: The problem is stark: your Null Sphere shield blocks magic and his damage is physical, and The Darkin Glaive (10s) is an auto-attack reset that heals him and recasts into a knock-up. Concede the trades, catch what CS you safely can, and lean on tower — every level survived without dying is a win.

edits.before: Level 6 restores some dignity: Riftwalk means he cannot run you down for free, though thin mana keeps any real fight a coin-flip — save the blink to escape, not to engage. If the denial worked and he has his item first, respect the tower-dive threat and demand jungle attention until you stabilise.
edits.after: Level 6 restores some dignity: Riftwalk means Aureate Rush (10s) cannot run you down for free, though thin mana keeps any fight a coin-flip. Grim Deliverance arrives with it — 110s at rank 1, and it heals him off its own damage, so never trade into a fresh one. Demand jungle attention until you stabilise.

notes: Highest-leverage matchup in the slice and it was the thinnest page: 1030 games, and not one of Zaahen's five abilities was named. Worse, the page fears the wrong one — it schedules your entire commit pattern around a 110s ultimate that has no crowd control, when the thing that actually catches a Riftwalk is a 14-second, 850-range pull. Two things for a human. First, the packet's enemyAbilities field is NULL for Zaahen while champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json is fully populated (key 904, Data Dragon 16.15.1) — whatever builds the packets is failing on this champion, which probably explains why the generic boilerplate was never filled in, and other Zaahen matchups across every lane are likely in the same state. Second, the revive on Cultivation of War is a power spike that runs on stacks rather than levels or items, so it has no natural home in a seven-stage level chart; I put it in the first-item spike because that is where the dive threat lives, but it deserves a considered placement.
